diagrams.title: The Vulnerability Management Loop
diagrams.subtitle: Identification → prioritization → remediation → verification → reporting. Click a step then test the order.

nodes.label: Identification
nodes.detail: Authenticated or unauthenticated scan, IPAM inventory, cloud posture CSPM, and source code review. Produces a list of candidate vulnerabilities, not a decision.
nodes.exam: IPAM and CSPM are outside the books: objective §4.3.

nodes.label: Prioritization
nodes.detail: Combines CVSS, exposure, asset criticality, and exploit availability. The pentest report provides proof of exploitability.
nodes.exam: A critical on an isolated asset may come after an exposed high: reason in context.

nodes.label: Remediation
nodes.detail: Patch, update, disable service, segment. If patching is impossible: compensating control and risk acceptance documented by the owner.
nodes.exam: 'We cannot patch' never justifies ignoring it: a written, dated exception is required.

nodes.label: Verification
nodes.detail: Re-scan with the same parameters to prove the vulnerability is gone before closing the ticket.
nodes.exam: Changing the scan method can make a finding disappear without fixing anything.

nodes.label: Reporting
nodes.detail: Internal reports to track SLAs, external reports for compliance obligations, bug bounty program and responsible disclosure to collaborate with researchers.
nodes.exam: Reporting feeds the prioritization of the next cycle: the loop is closed.

nodes.label: Accepted risk
nodes.detail: Alternative exit from remediation: the owner formally accepts the risk, with a compensating control and review date.
nodes.exam: An acceptance without a compensating control or expiration date is invalid.

quiz.question: Which step precedes verification and also precedes any risk acceptance?
